title: BigCommerce Developers
snippet:
### Create a sandbox store
Sign up for a free BigCommerce trial store to test API calls and build integrations without affecting live data.
### Generate API credentials
Navigate to **Settings > API Accounts** in your store control panel. Create credentials with the scopes you need.

title: API Accounts
snippet:
APIs](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/quick-start) that let you manage store data, authenticate customers, make client-side queries for product information, and more. API accounts are used to authenticate requests to our APIs.
There are two different API account types that can be created in the control panel: [store-level API accounts](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#store-level-api-accounts) that correspond to a single store, and [account-level API accounts](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#account-level-api-accounts) that function in all stores within your BigCommerce account.

### Requirements
- Only the [store owner](/articles/en_US/Knowledge/Store-Owner) can create account-level API accounts.
- To view, create, and manage store-level API accounts, you must be granted [high-risk user permissions](/articles/en_US/Knowledge/User-Permissions) by the store owner.
- To view webhooks, you must be granted the **Read Webhooks**[user permission](/articles/en_US/Knowledge/User-Permissions).

- **Subscriptions** — View or cancel [subscriptions](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/rest/storefront/subscriptions/create-subscription) to your store's marketing and abandoned cart emails.
- **Checkouts** — View or create [storefront checkouts](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/rest/storefront/checkouts).
- **Charges** — Create or delete charges via the [Payments API](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/rest/admin/payments).
- **Account** — View account information for Account level [GraphQL](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/storefront/guides/graphql-storefront-api/overview).
- **Account Stores** — View information for stores belonging to the account for Account level GraphQL.

Any apps intended for sale on the BigCommerce App Marketplace must use OAuth. OAuth is compatible with all current and planned BigCommerce APIs, including v2 Webhooks and our v3 API. For more information, see our documentation on [Authentication](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts) in our Developer Docs.

title: BigCommerce Docs
snippet:
BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce’s REST APIs: store-level credentials, app-level credentials, and account-level credentials. This section describes the difference between the three, how to obtain and revoke account credentials, and the use cases for each. It also contains a reference for available OAuth scopes and provides a compelling list of reasons to migrate from legacy API tokens to OAuth credentials.
Every parent set of API credentials that you request for your store is its own **API account**. At its simplest, an API account consists of the following:
- The `client_id` uniquely identifies the app or user, or the *client*, making a request.
- The `client_secret` is a cryptographically secure value known only to the client and BigCommerce.
Every active API account has at least one `access_token`. [Store-level API accounts](/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#store-level-api-accounts) include a static access token that does not change. [App-level API accounts](/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#app-level-api-accounts) expect each application to generate a unique access token for every store that installs the app. [Account-level API accounts](/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#account-level-api-accounts) include a single access token that belongs to the parent account of the store that the user is signed in to at the time of creation.

title: B2B Edition Overview
snippet:
Before you can start building a custom B2B solution, you’ll need a developer sandbox that can access our APIs. Use these steps to obtain the necessary tools and proceed with your development workflow.
### Create a Sandbox Store
To request a non-transactional sandbox store for development, fill out the form located in the “Create A Sandbox Store” step of the [BigCommerce API Overview](/developer/api-reference/about-our-apis). The developer sandbox is free of charge.
To request B2B Edition provisioning on your store, install the [B2B Edition app](https://www.bigcommerce.com/apps/b2b-edition/) from the marketplace and then [contact our support team](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/#contact) to start the process. If you are a [BigCommerce Partner](https://www.bigcommerce.com/partners/become-a-partner/), reach out to your partner manager to request B2B Edition.

You can [create an API account](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/article/B2B-Edition-Settings) from **Settings** > **API Accounts** in your B2B Edition control panel to authenticate requests to the REST Management API. You can also generate management and storefront tokens via API requests.

title: Beginning App Development
snippet:
Before you register and install a draft app, you need the following:
1. A BigCommerce store to test app installation. You can use any store you own. Partners can also create a [sandbox store](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/sandboxes).
2. A [Developer Portal](https://build.bigcommerce.com/) account (required to register apps).
3. A [BigCommerce partnership](https://www.bigcommerce.com/partners/) (required to publish apps to the App Marketplace). To apply, see [Becoming a partner](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/integrations/becoming-a-partner).
